keywords.description: Declares a reference type whose instances can contain data and behavior.
Declares a value type, copied by value unless used through a reference.
Declares a contract of members that implementing types must provide.
Declares a value type made from a named set of integral constants.
Declares a type-safe callable signature that can reference methods.
Declares a data-oriented class or struct with generated value-based features.
C# 15 preview: declares a type whose value is one of a fixed set of case types.
Alias for System.Boolean; stores true or false.
Alias for System.Byte; unsigned 8-bit integer.
Alias for System.SByte; signed 8-bit integer.
Alias for System.Int16; signed 16-bit integer.
Alias for System.UInt16; unsigned 16-bit integer.
Alias for System.Int32; signed 32-bit integer.
Alias for System.UInt32; unsigned 32-bit integer.
Alias for System.Int64; signed 64-bit integer.
Alias for System.UInt64; unsigned 64-bit integer.
Contextual alias for System.IntPtr; signed native-sized integer.
Contextual alias for System.UIntPtr; unsigned native-sized integer.
Alias for System.Char; one UTF-16 code unit.
Alias for System.Single; 32-bit floating-point value.
Alias for System.Double; 64-bit floating-point value.
Alias for System.Decimal; high-precision base-10 numeric value.
Alias for System.String; an immutable sequence of UTF-16 characters.
Alias for System.Object; the ultimate base type of .NET types.
Defers member binding and many type checks until runtime.
Indicates that a method returns no value, or represents an untyped pointer target.
Boolean literal representing the true value.
Boolean literal representing the false value.
Literal representing no object reference or no nullable value.
Produces the default value of a type; also labels a fallback switch case.
Makes a declared member or type accessible wherever its containing assembly is referenced.
Restricts access to the containing type.
Allows access from the containing type and derived types.
Restricts access to the same assembly.
Declares an incomplete type or member that must be completed by derivation or override.
Prevents a class from being inherited or an override from being overridden again.
Makes a member belong to the type itself, or declares a non-instantiable static class.
Allows an instance member to be overridden in a derived type.
Provides a new implementation of an inherited virtual or abstract member.
Restricts mutation of fields, structs, members, or references depending on context.
Applies special memory-access semantics to a field; it is not a replacement for locking.
Declares a compile-time constant whose value is embedded in consuming code.
Allows a type or supported member declaration to be split across multiple parts.
Requires callers to initialize a field or property during object creation.
Limits a top-level type to the source file in which it is declared.
C# 14: introduces an extension block containing extension members for another type.
C# 15 preview: restricts direct derived types to the declaring assembly for exhaustiveness analysis.
C# 15 preview: explicitly attests that a declaration is safe under the updated memory-safety model.
Declares the logical namespace that contains types or nested namespaces.
Introduces namespace imports, aliases, static imports, or deterministic resource disposal.
Refers to the global namespace or declares a project-wide global using directive.
Used with extern alias to reference an externally assigned assembly alias.
Creates an object or value; can also hide an inherited member or specify a constructor constraint.
Refers to the current instance; also marks an extension-method receiver or indexer parameter list.
Accesses base-class members or invokes a base-class constructor.
Produces the System.Type object for a type known at compile time.
Returns the size in bytes of an unmanaged type.
Produces a compile-time string containing the name of a symbol.
Allocates a block of memory on the stack, commonly exposed as a Span<T> or pointer.
Creates a modified copy or, in C# 15 collection expressions, supplies construction arguments.
Declares an event member with controlled subscription and unsubscription.
Defines the read accessor of a property or indexer.
Defines the write accessor of a property or indexer.
Defines a write accessor usable only during object initialization.
Defines the accessor executed when code subscribes to a custom event.
Defines the accessor executed when code unsubscribes from a custom event.
Implicit parameter containing the value supplied to a setter or custom event accessor.
C# 14: refers to a compiler-generated backing field inside a property accessor.
Declares a user-defined operator or conversion operator.
Declares a conversion that the compiler may apply without an explicit cast.
Declares a conversion that normally requires an explicit cast.
Tests a value against a type or pattern and can introduce a pattern variable.
Attempts a reference or nullable conversion and returns null when it fails.
Combines two patterns that must both match.
Combines alternative patterns where either may match.
Negates a pattern.
Executes a statement when a Boolean condition is true.
Provides the alternative branch of an if statement.
Selects a branch or value by matching cases or patterns.
Introduces a switch label or pattern arm.
Adds a filter to a catch clause or a guard to a switch case or arm.
Defines a loop with initializer, condition, and iterator components.
Iterates over elements produced by an enumerable pattern.
Repeats a statement while a condition remains true.
Starts a loop that evaluates its condition after each iteration.
Exits the nearest loop or switch; C# 15 preview also supports labeled targets.
Starts the next loop iteration; C# 15 preview also supports labeled targets.
Transfers control to a label, case label, or default label.
Exits a method, local function, lambda, or accessor and optionally supplies a value.
Produces the next value from an iterator or ends iterator production.
Introduces code whose exceptions may be handled or finalized.
Handles an exception thrown from an associated try block.
Runs cleanup code after try/catch completion regardless of success or exception.
Raises an exception or rethrows the current exception.
Enables overflow checking for integral arithmetic and conversions in a scope or expression.
Disables overflow checking for integral arithmetic and conversions in a scope or expression.
Executes a critical section with mutual exclusion on a synchronization object.
Allows a method parameter to accept a variable number of arguments or a parameter collection.
Marks a readonly by-reference parameter; also appears in foreach and query syntax.
Marks a by-reference output parameter that the callee must assign.
Passes, returns, or stores an alias to an existing variable or storage location.
Introduces generic constraints or filters elements in a LINQ query.
Constrains a generic type parameter to nonnullable types under nullable analysis.
Introduces an anti-constraint, currently used as allows ref struct for ref-like type arguments.
Restricts the escape lifetime of a ref-like parameter, local, or return value.
Marks a method, lambda, or anonymous function that can use await.
Suspends asynchronous execution until an awaitable operation completes without blocking the thread.
Introduces a query data source and range variable.
Projects query elements into the result sequence.
Groups query elements by a key.
Continues a query using the result of a group, join, or select clause.
Sorts query results by one or more keys.
Correlates elements from two data sources by matching keys.
Introduces a query range variable for a computed intermediate value.
Introduces the left key expression of a query join clause.
Separates the left and right key expressions of a query join clause.
Introduces the key expression of a group clause.
Requests ascending ordering for a query sort key.
Requests descending ordering for a query sort key.
Declares an externally implemented member or introduces an external assembly alias.
Permits pointer operations and other code requiring an unsafe context.
Pins managed storage for pointer access or declares a fixed-size buffer.
Specifies a managed function-pointer calling convention.
Specifies an unmanaged function-pointer convention or constrains T to unmanaged types.
Selects the C declaration unmanaged function-pointer calling convention.
Selects the Fastcall unmanaged function-pointer calling convention.
Selects the Standard Call unmanaged function-pointer calling convention.
Selects the Thiscall unmanaged function-pointer calling convention.
Requests compiler inference for a local variable type or captures a value in a var pattern.
Names the compiler-provided string[] command-line argument variable in top-level statements.
